content: SLURP1, or Secreted Ly-6/uPAR-related protein 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the SLURP1 gene. This protein exhibits anti-inflammatory properties and functions as a tumor suppressor. Additionally, it acts as an antagonist to nicotine. The protein encoded by the SLURP1 gene belongs to the Ly-6/uPAR family but notably lacks a GPI-anchoring signal sequence. It is secreted into the bloodstream and binds to the α7-acetylcholine receptor. Research has demonstrated that SLURP1 functions as an endogenous tumor suppressor by reducing cell migration and invasion. It achieves this by mediating its own anti-tumor effects and counteracting the pro-malignant effects of nicotine. Mutations in the SLURP1 gene have been linked to Mal de Meleda, a rare autosomal recessive skin disorder. This condition is characterized by inflammatory palmoplantar hyperkeratosis. The disorder arises from a loss of SLURP1 function, which leads to impaired epithelial differentiation and an increased secretion of inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL-1, IL-6, and IL-8. The SLURP1 gene is located in the same chromosomal region as several other members of the Ly-6/uPAR family of glycoprotein receptors.
